attacks.claim: The webhook receiver's grants omit SELECT, but it must read borrower_attributes and transport preferences to match phone numbers to patrons, read NOTICE_PREV, and write the staff circulation note. As written, the STOP and fallback paths cannot run.
attacks.evidence: "uses a dedicated DB user with UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`, and INSERT only on `message_queue` and `messages`"

attacks.claim: The no-lost-notices constraint depends entirely on delivery-failure callbacks reaching the receiver. The plan has no retry, buffering, or downtime alerting for the receiver, and no fallback when a callback never arrives. A failed SMS can therefore leave a patron with no notice.
attacks.evidence: "on an `undelivered`/`failed` status callback, the receiver queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel"; ABSENT: callback retry, receiver health alerting, handling of missing callbacks

attacks.claim: The provider-switch claim is contradicted elsewhere in the plan. The receiver verifies provider-specific signatures, STOP/HELP are provider-handled, and 10DLC brand and campaign registration is tied to the provider. Switching providers would require receiver and registration rework, not only a config change.
attacks.evidence: "Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change." vs "verifies the provider's request signature" and "brand registration approved Oct 14. The 'Library account notifications' campaign was submitted Oct 20"

attacks.claim: The message discloses that a specific patron has a filled request at a named branch with a count and expiry date. The statute bars disclosing requested materials, and the plan's claim that the text reveals nothing about what was requested is overstated. No counsel review of the message content is recorded; the Oct 1 review covers the contract clause.
attacks.evidence: "A reassigned number or shared phone reveals nothing about what the patron requested." and "the city attorney (Oct 1)" reviewed the contract clause; ABSENT: counsel sign-off on message body

attacks.claim: The provider retains the phone number with timestamps for 90 days. Combined with the library sender identity, this metadata links a number to library hold-notice activity, which the confidentiality statute may cover. Only message-body redaction is addressed.
attacks.evidence: "Message bodies are redacted at the provider after delivery; delivery metadata is kept 90 days per contract."

attacks.claim: Fallback for patrons whose NOTICE_PREV is phone routes failed texts to CallNotify, which ends 2027-03-31. The plan does not define the replacement, so after that date a failed SMS for a phone-prev patron has no working channel. This breaks the no-lost-notices constraint. The rollback has the same gap.
attacks.evidence: "queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel" and "restore `NOTICE_PREV` (email or phone call; print notice once CallNotify has ended)"

attacks.claim: 10DLC gating applies only to public launch. The week-3 pilot sends live traffic on an unapproved campaign, which carriers may filter or block, causing the pilot to produce misleading delivery data.
attacks.evidence: "Public launch is gated on approval." vs "Week 3: staff pilot. 40 staff cardholders opt in; we verify delivery"

attacks.claim: The public webhook POST path has no stated replay protection, signature secret storage, or parameterized-query requirement. Untrusted phone numbers and message IDs drive UPDATE and INSERT statements.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: replay protection, secret handling, query parameterization; "verifies the provider's request signature"

attacks.claim: The budget has no hard cap, only a $450 alert, and the uptake assumption is unvalidated. Confirmations, HELP/STOP replies, and fallback duplicates are not costed. The $600 limit is reached at about 52,800 texts/month, roughly 37% of hold volume.
attacks.evidence: "a provider spend alert fires at $450"; "Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons"

attacks.claim: The one-segment GSM-7 claim is unverified for Spanish. Accented characters such as á, í, ó and ú fall outside GSM-7, which would switch Spanish texts to UCS-2 and multi-segment billing. The Spanish template is not shown.
attacks.evidence: "Template (English, plus Spanish for patrons whose preferred language is Spanish, via `TranslateNotices`), GSM-7, one segment"

attacks.claim: NOTICE_PREV behaviour is undefined when a patron re-enrols or changes channel. Fallback 'consecutive failure' state has no storage. Re-enabling after STOP is also unaddressed, since provider-level blocks persist.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: NOTICE_PREV overwrite rules, failure-count storage, re-enrolment after STOP

attacks.claim: A STOP from one family member on a shared number silently switches every matching patron off SMS, including patrons who opted in on their own. This contradicts the per-patron opt-in model.
attacks.evidence: "switches every patron whose SMS number matches (family members can share a phone) from SMS back to their own `NOTICE_PREV`"

attacks.claim: Overnight-queued notices burst at 09:00 with no stated batch size, provider throughput cap, or 10DLC rate limit. The burst could exceed limits as volume grows.
attacks.evidence: "a hold filled after 20:00 is texted at 09:00"; ABSENT: batch size, throughput limits

attacks.claim: The 9.2% vs 5.1% expiry comparison is confounded by self-selection into SMS. The ≤5.5% target assumes SMS causes the improvement, and no holdout group is planned.
attacks.evidence: "Uncollected-hold expiry rate: 9.2% for phone-notice patrons vs 5.1% for email"; "Uncollected-hold expiry rate for SMS patrons ≤ 5.5%"

attacks.claim: Retention for circulation notes written to the messages table and for receiver logs is unspecified. Only message_queue has a 30-day purge.
attacks.evidence: "Koha `message_queue` rows are purged after 30 days"; ABSENT: retention for `messages` rows and receiver logs

attacks.claim: The STOP switch-back and the delivery-failure fallback both depend on one webhook receiver. The plan has no outage handling, no callback retry or dead-letter queue, and no alert on receiver health. If the receiver is down, STOP and failure callbacks are lost, and patrons keep getting SMS-blocked sends with no fallback. That breaks the agreed no-lost-notices constraint.
attacks.evidence: A webhook receiver (~150 lines, on the existing Koha app server behind the existing nginx/TLS) exposes a single rate-limited POST path ... ABSENT: receiver health alerting, callback retry, dead-letter handling

attacks.claim: Fallback and STOP routing send patrons to NOTICE_PREV=phone, but CallNotify ends 2027-03-31 and will not be renewed. The plan gives no rule for patrons whose NOTICE_PREV is phone after that date, so they lose hold notices. The rollback plan has the same gap.
attacks.evidence: new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`; ... restore `NOTICE_PREV` (email or phone call; print notice once CallNotify has ended)

attacks.claim: The rollback guarantee is contradicted by the enrolment rule. A new sign-up has no prior channel, so setting NOTICE_PREV to phone does not restore the channel they had before. The post-launch claim is false for that group.
attacks.evidence: Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before.

attacks.claim: The $600 cap has no hard enforcement. Spend exceeds $600 if email uptake passes about 32% at 50% phone uptake, or about 12% at full phone uptake. The $450 alert has no defined action. The uptake assumptions are not sourced, and the 64% survey figure measures preference, not uptake.
attacks.evidence: Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons ≈ 30,500 texts/month. ... a provider spend alert fires at $450.

attacks.claim: The $0.011 per-text rate is unsourced. The one-segment assumption is only shown for English. The Spanish template is not shown, and a non-GSM-7 Spanish body would drop to 70 characters and send as multiple segments, which would raise cost.
attacks.evidence: ~$0.011 per text including carrier fees; GSM-7, one segment; (Spanish template not shown)

attacks.claim: The template hard-codes the singular 'item' with a count variable. A patron with two or more holds filled gets grammatically wrong copy.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 1 item is ready for pickup at Eastside Branch until Nov 4." with count from notice template variables

attacks.claim: The body discloses that a library hold exists, with branch and pickup date, to whoever holds a reassigned or shared number. The plan's claim that this reveals nothing about the request is an unsupported legal conclusion. The city attorney reviewed the DPA and confidentiality clause, not the message text itself.
attacks.evidence: A reassigned number or shared phone reveals nothing about what the patron requested. ... a library-records confidentiality clause reviewed by the city attorney (Oct 1)

attacks.claim: Opt-out is not durably recorded in Koha. A STOP updates the preference and adds a circulation note, but the SMS_CONSENT attribute is not updated. The plan says opt-out records are kept so re-enabling never texts a STOP sender, but the only durable record is the provider's block, which Koha does not store.
attacks.evidence: adds a circulation note visible to staff; Patron attribute `SMS_CONSENT` records the date and source (opac/desk). ... Consent and opt-out records are kept, so re-enabling later never texts anyone who sent STOP.

attacks.claim: A new internet-facing POST endpoint on the Koha app host can perform patron-wide writes. The plan does not specify signature key handling, timestamp or replay protection, or behaviour on invalid requests. Its UPDATE grant on borrower_attributes is not limited to specific attribute codes.
attacks.evidence: verifies the provider's request signature ... UPDATE only on `borrower_message_transport_preferences` and `borrower_attributes`

attacks.claim: Sharing a phone number lets one patron's STOP switch every matching patron off SMS, including patrons who never opted out. It also silently stops another household member's SMS without notice to that member.
attacks.evidence: switches every patron whose SMS number matches (family members can share a phone) from SMS back to their own `NOTICE_PREV`

attacks.claim: The 9.2% vs 5.1% expiry gap is observational and confounded by patron mix, so it does not show SMS will reduce expiry. The ≤5.5% target has no baseline for SMS patrons.
attacks.evidence: Uncollected-hold expiry rate: 9.2% for phone-notice patrons vs 5.1% for email (Koha reports, Jan–Sep 2026). ... Uncollected-hold expiry rate for SMS patrons ≤ 5.5%

attacks.claim: The week-3 staff pilot is not gated on 10DLC approval, which may land around Nov 3–10. Unregistered traffic may be filtered, so pilot delivery results could be misleading.
attacks.evidence: Week 3: staff pilot. 40 staff cardholders opt in ... Public launch is gated on approval.

attacks.claim: Provider switching is not only a config change. The receiver's signature verification, the provider-side STOP and HELP handling, and the 10DLC brand and campaign registration are all provider-specific.
attacks.evidence: Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change.

attacks.claim: The plan does not address provider or 10DLC campaign throughput limits, or the single receiver path, at 10x volume.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: throughput limits for the campaign and provider, and receiver capacity at 10x volume

attacks.claim: Each hold triggers its own text, so a patron with several holds filled the same day receives several texts. There is no batching or digest.
attacks.evidence: Template ... "1 item is ready for pickup" sent per filled hold; no batching rule

attacks.claim: New sign-ups and all SMS patrons have their fallback and STOP-revert channel set to `phone`, but CallNotify ends 2027-03-31 and calls are out of scope (LIBSYS-330). After that date, STOP or repeated delivery failure silently strands the patron on a dead channel, which breaks the agreed 'no patron may lose hold notices' constraint.
attacks.evidence: "(new sign-ups who pick SMS get `phone`; every SMS patron has a mobile number)"; "print notice once CallNotify has ended"; "Out: ... what replaces calls for patrons who stay on phone after March 2027 (LIBSYS-330)"

attacks.claim: The claim that patrons end up on the channel they had before is false for new sign-ups, whose prior channel is nothing and whose NOTICE_PREV is set to `phone`. The rollback and STOP paths therefore do not restore a working channel for them.
attacks.evidence: "Patrons who enrolled after launch end up on exactly the channel they had before."

attacks.claim: The text and the provider flow reveal hold status (count, branch, pickup date) tied to a phone number, and a shared phone exposes this to other household members. The plan asserts the message reveals nothing about requests, which is contradicted by the content. No city-attorney review of the message body is evidenced; the attorney reviewed only the DPA/confidentiality clause.
attacks.evidence: "A reassigned number or shared phone reveals nothing about what the patron requested."; "a library-records confidentiality clause reviewed by the city attorney (Oct 1)"

attacks.claim: The provider receives phone numbers linked to library hold events, and that linkage is retained for 90 days of delivery metadata. The plan does not justify this linkage against the statute or limit it, and the data residency of the provider is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "The provider receives only the phone number and the message body above."; "delivery metadata is kept 90 days per contract"

attacks.claim: New mobile numbers are collected and stored in Koha, but the plan gives no retention or deletion rule for them after STOP or when a patron leaves SMS. Koha's `messages` table, which the receiver INSERTs into, has no stated purge.
attacks.evidence: "Koha `message_queue` rows are purged after 30 days by the existing `cleanup_database.pl` job (unchanged)." (no rule for `messages` or the SMS_CONSENT/mobile number attribute)

attacks.claim: The webhook is an internet-facing write path into patron preferences, message_queue and messages. The plan names signature verification but not the key source, rotation, or replay protection. A forged or replayed callback could insert notices or flip channels.
attacks.evidence: "exposes a single rate-limited POST path, verifies the provider's request signature, then:"

attacks.claim: The hold-notice guarantee depends entirely on provider status callbacks reaching a single rate-limited endpoint. Dropped callbacks (rate limiting), a receiver outage, or a missed callback mean no fallback fires and the hold notice is lost. The plan has no timeout-based fallback, reconciliation, or alert on receiver health.
attacks.evidence: "on an `undelivered`/`failed` status callback, the receiver queues the same notice on the patron's `NOTICE_PREV` channel"; "exposes a single rate-limited POST path"; no alerting described

attacks.claim: The plan says switching providers is a config change, but the receiver is provider-specific (signature scheme, callback format, keyword handling), and STOP blocks, 10DLC registration and the DPA are all provider-held. Exit cost is understated.
attacks.evidence: "Switching providers later is a config change, not a code change."

attacks.claim: Spend is not capped. A spend alert at $450 does not stop sends. Spend reaches the $600 budget at roughly 54,500 texts/month, about 1.8x the assumed 30,500. Uptake is an unvalidated assumption, and fallback sends to CallNotify add unpriced cost.
attacks.evidence: "Approved notices budget allows up to $600/month for SMS (finance memo FIN-2026-117); a provider spend alert fires at $450."; "Assumed uptake: 50% of phone patrons + 10% of email patrons"

attacks.claim: The cost model and the 'one segment' claim depend on GSM-7 single-segment messages. The Spanish template is not written and not tested, and Spanish accented vowels are likely outside GSM-7 (forcing UCS-2 at 70 chars per segment). Two segments per Spanish text would raise cost and could breach the budget.
attacks.evidence: "Template (English, plus Spanish for patrons whose preferred language is Spanish, via `TranslateNotices`), GSM-7, one segment:"

attacks.claim: The staff pilot in week 3 sends A2P texts before the 10DLC campaign is approved, while the plan gates only public launch. Unregistered traffic is commonly blocked by carriers, so the pilot cannot validate delivery and may itself violate carrier rules.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: staff pilot. 40 staff cardholders opt in"; "Public launch is gated on approval."

attacks.claim: The 5.5% expiry target for SMS patrons assumes SMS patrons behave like email patrons. This is unprototyped and compares self-selected SMS users with phone patrons, and the 9.2% baseline is for phone patrons overall.
attacks.evidence: "Uncollected-hold expiry rate for SMS patrons ≤ 5.5% (phone today: 9.2%)"

attacks.claim: The count variable in the single text is asserted to come from template variables with no prototype. Koha hold-filled notices are typically generated per hold, so a patron with several holds could receive several texts, which the cost model does not price.
attacks.evidence: "Count, branch and date come from notice template variables; the per-item title loop used in the email template is deliberately left out."

attacks.claim: STOP handling matches all patrons on a shared SMS number, and no index or query cost is described for patron-attribute lookups at 180,000 cardholders. A STOP storm or a mass number-sharing event is not bounded.
attacks.evidence: "switches every patron whose SMS number matches"

attacks.claim: A custom ~150-line webhook, a dedicated DB user with a split UPDATE/INSERT grant, and a rollback script add hidden coupling to Koha internals and provider semantics, with no test plan for the receiver beyond the pilot.
attacks.evidence: "A webhook receiver (~150 lines, on the existing Koha app server behind the existing nginx/TLS)"
